title: Icepack: initialize from HDF5
chapter_timing: Receipt-bound logical chapters include control cue, actual transition and confirmation; durations are video times.

steps.title: Your goal: initialize and run Icepack
instructions: Run a synthetic shelf from your own gridded fields, then save the initial/final maps and native results.
Download run.py, initial_fields.py and icepack-shelf-initial.h5 from this tutorial page.
Open CryoLauncher and sign in. Use an approved connected cloud account with its resources prepared.
The following steps select this tutorial’s model and example.
steps.why: Keep the source inputs, inspect native fields, and save a complete result package. An owned example keeps scripts, dataset references and results together.
steps.expected: Your workspace keeps scripts, datasets, run history and results together.
steps.note: Start with your approved cloud account already connected and its cloud resources prepared. Shared application orientation; the case-specific configuration follows.

steps.title: 1. Open the cloud workspace
instructions: Choose Cloud → Advanced → Icepack.
You will create a separate workspace example for this HDF5 run.
Choose Icepack as the model.
Next, create a new owned workspace example with a separate name for this HDF5 run.
steps.why: Cloud uses your connected account; Advanced enables your owned scripts and datasets. The selected example controls the source files and dataset references used for launch.
steps.expected: The next step gives your HDF5 run a separate name.
steps.note: Keep the three supplied tutorial files together on your computer.

steps.title: 2. Create your own example
instructions: Enter a new name, then choose New example.
The new example has an empty file list, ready for your Python files.
steps.why: An owned workspace separates your files from the supplied application example.
steps.expected: Wait for the created-workspace message and empty file list.

steps.title: 3. Select both Python files
instructions: Choose script files. In your file picker, select run.py and initial_fields.py, then choose Open.
Check that the button now shows two selected files.
steps.why: Selection picks local files; importing is the step that saves them in this example.
steps.expected: Check that two script files are selected.
steps.note: You will import both files into the same workspace example.

steps.title: 4. Import the selected scripts
instructions: Choose Import script files.
Wait for Imported run.py, initial_fields.py. Files are saved.
The file selector now contains run.py; the import confirmation lists both imported files.
steps.why: Import saves the selected source files; it does not submit a model run.
steps.expected: Expected: Imported run.py, initial_fields.py. Files are saved.
steps.note: If your example already contains run.py, enable Replace existing script files first. For seeded or existing files, use Replace existing script files before importing.

steps.title: 5. Use run.py as the entry point
instructions: Set Run target to run.py.
This script calls initial_fields.py to validate and read your HDF5 input.
steps.why: Run target selects the entry script; other imported files can act as helpers.
steps.expected: The script calls initial_fields.py to read and validate your HDF5 input.
steps.note: Importing files saves them; launching is a separate step.

steps.title: 6. Choose your HDF5 input
instructions: In Datasets choose Choose data files.
In your file picker select icepack-shelf-initial.h5 and choose Open. Check that one file is selected.
steps.why: Selecting a file prepares it for upload; it is not in the dataset registry yet.
steps.expected: Check that one data file is selected.
steps.note: Next, upload the selected file into your workspace.

steps.title: 7. Upload the selected data file
instructions: Choose Upload. Wait for Uploaded: icepack-shelf-initial.h5.
Check that the new HDF5 filename appears in your dataset list.
steps.why: Upload stores the dataset; the script must read its fields to initialize the model.
steps.note: The supplied file contains full thickness, base, surface, vx, vy and floating-mask grids.

steps.title: 8. Reference the file in this example
instructions: Select icepack-shelf-initial.h5. Keep that filename as the reference alias, then choose Reference in example.
Read the reference confirmation: data/icepack-shelf-initial.h5.
When you launch, CryoLauncher copies the selected dataset into that path for run.py to read.
steps.why: A reference stages the chosen dataset under data/ when this example launches.
steps.note: Your script will read data/icepack-shelf-initial.h5. The reference is attached to your current workspace example.

steps.title: 9. Review your configuration
instructions: Choose Review & Launch.
Before submitting, check that the summary names your intended model and workspace example.
Check Model: ICEPACK and Example: pilot-icepack-h5-1118.
Keep run.py as the entry point, with the referenced HDF5 input attached.
Choose Launch cloud run when the readiness checks are ready.
Your HDF5 run now has its own Cloud Run card.
Wait for the job to finish; opening another tab does not cancel it.
steps.why: Review is the checkpoint for the selected case, inputs, resources and charges. Confirm the intended model and owned example before submitting the run. Confirmation starts a paid cloud run using the reviewed configuration. Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.
steps.expected: Wait for completion; opening another tab does not cancel the job.
steps.note: Review the current settings before you launch. This native run used 2 vCPU and 8 GiB. Control guide; the original accepted HDF5 run follows. This run used 2 vCPU and 8 GiB. Queue/startup and model timings are reported separately.

steps.title: 10. Open the completed results
instructions: When the run shows Completed, open View results.
The native script performs one 0.01-year step with zero accumulation.
steps.why: Completion lets you retrieve and inspect this run’s saved native output.
steps.expected: This script runs one 0.01-year step with zero accumulation.
steps.note: Next, render and save the fields from this completed HDF5 run.

steps.title: 11. Render a native field
instructions: Choose Render to draw the selected field.
In Results choose solution icepack, choose velocity or thickness, then choose Render.
Use the field name and units to interpret the plot.
steps.why: The solution, field name and units identify what you are about to view. The solution, field name and units identify what you are viewing.
steps.expected: Velocity is in metres/year; thickness is in metres.
steps.note: You can switch between thickness and velocity after the run finishes. Velocity is in metres/year; thickness is in metres.

steps.title: 12. Inspect the initialized fields
instructions: Open initial-conditions.png in your saved results.
It shows thickness, surface and speed sampled from your uploaded grid onto the native mesh.
steps.why: The saved initial map lets you inspect what was sampled from the uploaded grid.
steps.expected: The uploaded 5 × 9 grid was sampled at all 25 native mesh vertices.
steps.note: The supplied grid has 5 × 9 points and covers a 10 km × 10 km synthetic shelf.

steps.title: 13. Inspect the final thickness
instructions: Open the final thickness figure and compare the colour scale with the initial map.
Final thickness is 300.022696–499.980847 m; its area-weighted mean is 403.649861 m.
steps.why: Use the colour scale and units to interpret the solved native thickness.
steps.expected: Final area-weighted mean: 403.649861 m; domain RMS speed: 133.908461 m/year.
steps.note: The final domain RMS speed is 133.908461 m/year.

steps.title: 14. Generate your download link
instructions: Choose Download results.
Wait for a new HTTPS download link for the current run.
Open the generated HTTPS link to save your results ZIP.
It contains the mesh, native fields, initial/final figures, metrics and runtime/RNG provenance.
steps.why: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.
steps.expected: Keep all 12 archive members with your scripts and HDF5 input.
steps.note: Use the freshly generated link to save the ZIP. Keep this 12-member archive and its manifest with your input files.

steps.title: What this completed example establishes
instructions: The five initialized fields matched an independent interpolation at all 25 native nodes; the mesh has 32 triangles.
These portable CG1 fields are numeric results, rather than a Firedrake checkpoint. This example is not an independent native repeat or an accuracy assessment.
steps.why: Keep the scientific qualifications and provenance with the accepted result.
steps.expected: Initial-field interpolation matched independently at every native node.
steps.note: Submission → Batch start: 214.703 s; task: 46.352 s; script: 16.9818 s. Long waits are shortened in the video.
